claim: The salivary gland tubes in Drosophila embryos form from a flat, nearly circular epithelial primordium called the salivary gland placode.
source: The symmetrical tubes of the embryonic salivary glands form from a flat, nearly circular epithelial primordium, the salivary gland placode (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The invagination point in the salivary gland placode is positioned asymmetrically in the dorsal-posterior corner rather than in the center.
source: Interestingly, the point of invagination from the circular placode primordium is not in the center of the placode, but in an asymmetric, eccentric position in the dorsal-posterior corner (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A showing the asymmetric positioning.

claim: Early apical constriction and cell wedging at the invagination pit initiates tissue bending in the salivary gland placode.
source: Using quantitative morphometric methods, we showed that the early apical constriction and associated cell wedging at the position of the invagination pit initiates the tissue bending (Booth et al., 2014; Sanchez-Corrales et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Isotropic constriction driven by apical-medial actomyosin is concentrated near the forming invagination pit.
source: Isotropic constriction driven by apical-medial actomyosin is concentrated near the forming invagination pit (Figure 1A' and A'')
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 1A' and A'' showing the distribution of actomyosin.

claim: Cell intercalation driven by polarised junctional actomyosin dominates at a distance from the invagination pit.
source: but at a distance to the pit a second cell behavior dominates cell intercalation. Driven by a polarised junctional accumulation of actomyosin, cell intercalation events such as T1 exchanges and rosette formation and resolution help to elongate the tissue radially toward the invagination pit and contract it circumferentially, via circumferential neighbor gains (Figure 1A'; Sanchez-Corrales et al., 2018).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 1A' and a citation to previous work.

claim: Cells near the invagination pit continuously constrict until they are internalized.
source: Note that cells near the pit continuously constrict until internalized (pink shaded box), whereas cells far from the pit do not constrict significantly until t=20 min whilst moving closer to the pit (gray shaded box), but once they are in close proximity to the pit they also constrict until internalized (blue shaded box).
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 1E and supported by the data shown in the figure.

claim: Cells initially positioned far from the pit do not constrict significantly until approximately t=20 min when they move closer to the pit.
source: Note that cells near the pit continuously constrict until internalized (pink shaded box), whereas cells far from the pit do not constrict significantly until t=20 min whilst moving closer to the pit (gray shaded box), but once they are in close proximity to the pit they also constrict until internalized (blue shaded box).
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 1E and supported by the data shown in the figure.

claim: Cells far from the pit switch to apical constriction behavior once they are in close proximity to the pit.
source: Note that cells near the pit continuously constrict until internalized (pink shaded box), whereas cells far from the pit do not constrict significantly until t=20 min whilst moving closer to the pit (gray shaded box), but once they are in close proximity to the pit they also constrict until internalized (blue shaded box).
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 1E and supported by the data shown in the figure.

claim: In hkb−/− mutants where a more central invagination forms, the overall morphogenesis is disrupted and the invaginated structure is sack-like and irregular.
source: An indication that the asymmetry of the salivary gland placode is important for wild-type tube formation is given by the reports that in certain mutant situations where a more central invagination appears to form, the overall morphogenesis is disrupted and the invaginated structure that forms is sack-like and irregular. This is true for embryos lacking the transcription factor Hkb that is expressed early in the placode (Myat and Andrew, 2000b; Myat and Andrew, 2002), and could therefore potentially implicate Hkb in establishing early placode patterning.
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The transcription factor Forkhead (Fkh) is initially expressed in the dorsal posterior region of the placode.
source: Previous studies have shown that several proteins known to be expressed in the placode can be detected at the mRNA level initially in the dorsal posterior region of the placode. These include the transcription factor Forkhead (Fkh) (Myat and Andrew, 2000a)
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The dynein-associated protein Klar is initially expressed in the dorsal posterior region of the placode.
source: Previous studies have shown that several proteins known to be expressed in the placode can be detected at the mRNA level initially in the dorsal posterior region of the placode. These include the transcription factor Forkhead (Fkh) (Myat and Andrew, 2000a), the dynein-associated protein Klar (Myat and Andrew, 2002)
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The kinase Btk29 is initially expressed in the dorsal posterior region of the placode.
source: Previous studies have shown that several proteins known to be expressed in the placode can be detected at the mRNA level initially in the dorsal posterior region of the placode. These include the transcription factor Forkhead (Fkh) (Myat and Andrew, 2000a), the dynein-associated protein Klar (Myat and Andrew, 2002), as well as the kinase Btk29 (Chandrasekaran and Beckendorf, 2005).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: fkh−/− mutants fail to apically constrict in the dorsal-posterior corner.
source: In agreement with this, we previously found that fkh−/− mutants specifically fail to apically constrict in the dorsal-posterior corner, though they do show intercalation behavior, and these mutants do not invaginate a tube (Sanchez-Corrales et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: fkh−/− mutants show intercalation behavior despite failing to apically constrict.
source: In agreement with this, we previously found that fkh−/− mutants specifically fail to apically constrict in the dorsal-posterior corner, though they do show intercalation behavior, and these mutants do not invaginate a tube (Sanchez-Corrales et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: fkh−/− mutants do not invaginate a tube.
source: In agreement with this, we previously found that fkh−/− mutants specifically fail to apically constrict in the dorsal-posterior corner, though they do show intercalation behavior, and these mutants do not invaginate a tube (Sanchez-Corrales et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Apical constriction is always strongest near the invagination pit at any moment in time.
source: We found that apical constriction is always strongest near the invagination pit at any moment in time.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a finding from the study.

claim: As coronae of cells approach the region near the pit, they switch behavior from predominantly intercalating to predominantly apically constricting/wedging.
source: As more and more coronae of cells approach the region near the pit, they switch behavior from predominantly intercalating to predominantly apically constricting/wedging.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a finding from the study.

claim: The continued near-pit constriction is driven by apical-medial myosin whose peak intensity and pulsatile strength is tracked in a fixed position close to the pit over time.
source: The continued near-pit constriction is driven by apical-medial myosin, whose peak intensity and peak pulsatile strength is tracked in a fixed position close to the pit over time.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a finding from the study.

claim: Hkb and Fkh expression levels pre-pattern where initial constriction occurs.
source: Using live-imaging of endogenous fluorescently tagged versions of Hkb and Fkh, we show that their expression levels pre-pattern where initial constriction is occurring.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a finding from the study.

claim: Hkb and Fkh are upstream of a dynamic patterning of the GPCR ligand Fog.
source: Both are upstream of a dynamic patterning of the GPCR ligand Fog, that in turn activates apical-medial myosin.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a finding from the study.

claim: Fog activates apical-medial myosin.
source: Both are upstream of a dynamic patterning of the GPCR ligand Fog, that in turn activates apical-medial myosin.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a finding from the study.

claim: Loss of correct pre-patterning in hkb−/− mutants leads to loss of symmetrical final organ shape with a narrow lumen.
source: Loss of the correct pre-patterning, such as in hkb−/− mutants or when Fog is overexpressed, leads to loss of the symmetrical final organ shape with a narrow lumen and instead gives rise to expanded and sack-like glands with widened lumena.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a finding from the study.

claim: Overexpression of Fog leads to loss of symmetrical final organ shape with a narrow lumen.
source: Loss of the correct pre-patterning, such as in hkb−/− mutants or when Fog is overexpressed, leads to loss of the symmetrical final organ shape with a narrow lumen and instead gives rise to expanded and sack-like glands with widened lumena.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a finding from the study.

claim: Loss of correct pre-patterning gives rise to expanded and sack-like glands with widened lumena.
source: Loss of the correct pre-patterning, such as in hkb−/− mutants or when Fog is overexpressed, leads to loss of the symmetrical final organ shape with a narrow lumen and instead gives rise to expanded and sack-like glands with widened lumena.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a finding from the study.

claim: Cells positioned near the pit at t=0 min constricted their apices isotropically and rapidly and were internalized by about t=+20 min.
source: Cells positioned near the pit at t=0 min (Figure 1B, pink) constricted their apices isotropically and rapidly and were internalized by about t=+ 20 min (Figure 1B and C and dashed curve in Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 1B, 1C, and 1E.

claim: Cells positioned far from the pit at t=0 min began constricting as they moved into a position closer to the invagination point.
source: Cells positioned far from the pit at t=0 min (Figure 1B, gray) and moving into a position closer to the invagination point began constricting (Figure 1B and D and solid curve in Figure 1E; Figure 1—video 1), suggesting that cells changed their behavior depending on where they were positioned in the placode with respect to the invagination point.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 1B, 1D, and 1E.

claim: Cells change their behavior depending on where they are positioned in the placode with respect to the invagination point.
source: Cells positioned far from the pit at t=0 min (Figure 1B, gray) and moving into a position closer to the invagination point began constricting (Figure 1B and D and solid curve in Figure 1E; Figure 1—video 1), suggesting that cells changed their behavior depending on where they were positioned in the placode with respect to the invagination point.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 1B, 1D, and 1E.

claim: Cells near the pit displayed isotropic constriction and a negative cumulative apical area change from the start.
source: Cells near the pit displayed isotropic constriction and thus a negative cumulative apical area change from the start (Figure 1E, pink highlighted)
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 1E.

claim: Cells initially positioned far from the pit retained their apical area initially and only began constricting from t>+20 min onwards.
source: whereas cells initially positioned far from the pit did not change their apical area over the first ~20 min (Figure 1C, gray highlighted), but then began to display isotropic apical constriction (Figure 1E, blue highlighted).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 1C and 1E.

claim: Cells far from the pit initially showed predominantly cell intercalation behavior that constricts the tissue primordium circumferentially whilst expanding it radially.
source: As described previously (Sanchez-Corrales et al., 2018), cells far from the pit initially showed predominantly a cell intercalation behavior that constricts the tissue primordium circumferentially whilst expanding it radially, thereby moving cells closer to the invagination pit (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text, supported by Figure 1G, and cites previous work.

claim: Cell intercalation moves cells closer to the invagination pit.
source: As described previously (Sanchez-Corrales et al., 2018), cells far from the pit initially showed predominantly a cell intercalation behavior that constricts the tissue primordium circumferentially whilst expanding it radially, thereby moving cells closer to the invagination pit (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text, supported by Figure 1G, and cites previous work.

claim: An initially pre-patterned behavior is dynamically adjusted during tube budding so that cells within a similar distance to the invagination pit display the same behavior.
source: These data strongly suggest that an initially pre-patterned behavior, isotropic constriction at the pit and intercalation further away, is dynamically adjusted during tube budding from a flat epithelial sheet, so that cells within a similar distance to the invagination pit display the same behavior.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as an interpretation of the data presented.

claim: Early apical constriction at the pit is driven by a highly dynamic apical-medial actomyosin network.
source: Early apical constriction at the pit is driven by a highly dynamic apical-medial actomyosin network (Booth et al., 2014; Sanchez-Corrales et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Cells near the future invagination point at t=0 min showed strong accumulation of apical-medial myosin.
source: cells near the future invagination point at t=0 min showed strong accumulation of apical-medial myosin (Figure 2A, A'' and C; see also Figure 2—video 1)
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 2A, A'', and C.

claim: Cells far from the pit and close to the anterior placode boundary showed mainly junctional myosin II accumulation at t=0 min.
source: whereas cells far from the pit and close to the anterior placode boundary (Figure 2A and A') showed mainly junctional myosin II accumulation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 2A and A'.

claim: At t=30 min, cells located right next to the invagination pit continued to display strong apical-medial myosin accumulation.
source: At t=30 min, the cells now located right next to the invagination pit continued to display strong apical-medial myosin accumulation (Figure 2B and B'')
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 2B and B''.

claim: Cells that were initially far from the pit but moved closer to it started to display apical-medial actomyosin at t=30 min.
source: but in addition cells that were initially 'far from the pit,' but were now in a closer proximity to the pit though still near the anterior boundary, now also started to display apical-medial actomyosin (Figure 2B and B').
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 2B and B'.

claim: Being moved into a position near the invagination pit determines levels of apical-medial myosin accumulation.
source: Thus, being moved into a position near the invagination pit appeared to determine levels of apical-medial myosin accumulation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as an interpretation of the data.

claim: The peak of apical-medial myosin fluorescence intensity tracked in a near-fixed position to the edge of the pit over time.
source: Looking placode-wide over the whole time period analyzed, the peak of the apical-medial myosin fluorescence intensity tracked in a near-fixed position to the edge of the pit over time (Figure 2D, white dotted line).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 2D.

claim: The location of the highest medial myosin intensity was where cells showed the shortest cycle lengths of medial myosin II fluctuations.
source: The location of the highest medial myosin intensity was also where cells showed the shortest cycle lengths of medial myosin II fluctuations (Figure 2E, white dotted line).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 2E.

claim: Cells near the pit at t=0 min showed an overall shorter myosin II cycle length compared to cells located far from the pit.
source: Interestingly, cells near the pit at t=0 min showed an overall shorter myosin II cycle length (the time period elapsed between two peaks of highest myosin II intensity during the oscillation, see schematic in Figure 2E) compared to cells located far from the pit (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 2E and 2F.

claim: Longer myosin II cycle length correlates with unproductive myosin cycles.
source: As longer cycle length correlates with unproductive myosin cycles (Booth et al., 2014), this was in line with cells further away from the pit showing less apical constriction.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Myosin strength across the placode at t=0 min was much higher in cells near the invagination point with a gradual decrease toward the placode boundary.
source: This myosin strength across the placode at t=0 min was much higher in cells near the invagination point when plotted against the distance to the pit, with a gradual decrease in myosin strength toward the placode boundary (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 2G.

claim: Cells originally far from the pit at t=0 min increased their myosin strength over time whilst moving into a position closer to the pit.
source: However, cells originally far from the pit at t=0 min increased their myosin strength over time (and concomitantly decreased their cycle length; see Figure 2—figure supplement 1) whilst moving into a position closer to the pit, so that by t=55 min their myosin strength had increased to levels previously shown by cells near the pit at t=0 min (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The early asymmetric setup of high apical-medial myosin II intensity and activity clustered near the pit was maintained during the continued invagination of the tube.
source: Thus, our data show that the early asymmetric setup of high apical-medial myosin II intensity and activity that was clustered near the pit was maintained during the continued invagination of the tube, in turn driving the continued apical constriction near the pit.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a conclusion from the data.

claim: The maintained asymmetric setup of myosin II drives the continued apical constriction near the pit.
source: Thus, our data show that the early asymmetric setup of high apical-medial myosin II intensity and activity that was clustered near the pit was maintained during the continued invagination of the tube, in turn driving the continued apical constriction near the pit.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a conclusion from the data.

claim: hkb−/− mutants show a central invagination pit compared to the eccentric pit in wild-type placodes.
source: A possibly more interesting situation is present in a previously published mutant of the transcription factor Huckebein (Hkb) that was reported to show a central invagination pit, combined with malformed invaginated salivary glands at later stages (Myat and Andrew, 2000b; Myat and Andrew, 2002).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: hkb−/− mutants show malformed invaginated salivary glands at later stages.
source: A possibly more interesting situation is present in a previously published mutant of the transcription factor Huckebein (Hkb) that was reported to show a central invagination pit, combined with malformed invaginated salivary glands at later stages (Myat and Andrew, 2000b; Myat and Andrew, 2002).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In hkb−/− mutant embryos at t~+40 min, no invagination had occurred yet, whereas in wild-type embryos most secretory cells had already invaginated.
source: Whereas in wild-type embryos, at t ~ +40 min, most secretory cells of the salivary gland placode have already invaginated (Figure 3A''', B''' and C'''), in the hkb−/− mutants no invagination had occurred yet (Figure 3D''', E''' and F''').
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 3A''', B''', C''', D''', E''', and F'''.

claim: hkb−/− mutant embryos eventually invaginated a dilated tube through an enlarged pit.
source: Eventually, these embryos invaginated a dilated tube through an enlarged pit (see Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: In wild-type placodes, the area of strongest apical area constriction was always located in a position near the pit.
source: In the wild-type, the area of strongest apical area constriction was always located in a position near the pit, similar to the distribution of medial myosin intensity and activity (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 2D and 2E.

claim: In hkb−/− mutant placodes, cells began to constrict in an aberrant central position from about t=+20–30 min.
source: In contrast, in hkb−/− mutant placodes cells began to constrict in an aberrant central position from about t=+20–30 min (Figure 3G and H).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 3G and 3H.

claim: hkb−/− mutants show a delayed central invagination pit compared to the eccentric pit observed in wild-type placodes.
source: Thus, hkb−/− mutants show a delayed central invagination pit compared to the eccentric pit observed in wild-type placodes (Figure 3(I)1').
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 3I1'.

claim: Cells in hkb−/− mutant placodes located near the central pit started to constrict at a much slower rate than cells in wild-type placodes, and only from about t=+20 min on.
source: This analysis showed that cells in hkb−/− mutant placodes located near the central pit started to constrict at a much slower rate than cells in wild-type placodes, and only from about t=+20 min on (Figure 3J, wild-type data reproduced from Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 3J.

claim: The rate of constriction of central cells in hkb−/− mutants was very similar to that of cells located at a distance to the pit in wild-type.
source: In fact, the rate of the constriction of the central cells in hkb−/− mutants was very similar to that of the cells located at a distance to the pit in the wild-type (compare blue dashed and magenta solid curves), suggesting that the central cells in hkb−/− mutants continue to behave identical to the wild-type cells occupying the same position.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by the comparison of curves in Figure 3J.

claim: Central cells in hkb−/− mutants continue to behave identically to wild-type cells occupying the same position.
source: In fact, the rate of the constriction of the central cells in hkb−/− mutants was very similar to that of the cells located at a distance to the pit in the wild-type (compare blue dashed and magenta solid curves), suggesting that the central cells in hkb−/− mutants continue to behave identical to the wild-type cells occupying the same position.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Cells far from the central pit in hkb−/− mutants showed a slight apical area expansion up to t=+20 min followed by a slight constriction.
source: Cells far from the central pit in hkb−/− mutants showed a slight apical area expansion up to t=+20 min followed by a slight constriction, but did not invaginate over the time interval shown in the plots.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by the data in Figure 3J.

claim: Cells far from the central pit in hkb−/− mutants did not invaginate over the time interval analyzed.
source: Cells far from the central pit in hkb−/− mutants showed a slight apical area expansion up to t=+20 min followed by a slight constriction, but did not invaginate over the time interval shown in the plots.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by the data in Figure 3J.

claim: hkb−/− mutant placodes showed no accumulation of apical-medial actomyosin at the eccentric position where a pit forms in wild-type.
source: In agreement with the delayed central constriction of cells in hkb−/− mutant placodes, we found no accumulation of apical-medial actomyosin at the eccentric position where a pit forms in the wild-type (compare Figure 3E and K to Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by comparing Figures 3E, 3K, and 2D.

claim: At t~+40 min, a central group of cells in hkb−/− mutant placodes displayed increased accumulation of apical-medial myosin II.
source: Instead, only at t~+40 min did a central group of cells in hkb−/− mutant placodes display increased accumulation of apical-medial myosin II (Figure 3K), inducing a shallow tissue bending in this region at this point (see also Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 3K and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Increased accumulation of apical-medial myosin II in hkb−/− mutants induced a shallow tissue bending in the central region.
source: Instead, only at t~+40 min did a central group of cells in hkb−/− mutant placodes display increased accumulation of apical-medial myosin II (Figure 3K), inducing a shallow tissue bending in this region at this point (see also Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 3K and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: In comparison to wild-type placode with an eccentric invagination, in hkb−/− mutant placodes a central invagination formed with a significant delay in time.
source: Thus, in comparison to wild-type placode with an eccentric invagination, in hkb−/− mutant placodes a central invagination formed with a significant delay in time.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a summary of the findings.

claim: The initial asymmetrical setup of cell behaviors in the placode is disrupted in hkb−/− embryos.
source: The above analyses strongly suggest that the initial asymmetrical setup of cell behaviors in the placode might be disrupted in hkb−/− embryos.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as an interpretation of the data.

claim: In wild-type placodes, cells near the eccentric invagination pit constricted isotropically with near equal change in strain at the tissue and cell shape level and very little intercalation strain.
source: In wild-type placodes, cells that were located near the eccentric invagination pit (Figure 4A; with the 'near' position defined at t=0 min; see also Figure 4—figure supplement 1) constricted isotropically, with near equal change in strain at the tissue and cell shape level, and very little intercalation strain (Figure 4A' and A'', solid curves).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 4A, 4A', and 4A''.

claim: Cells near the eccentric pit in wild-type placodes had all invaginated by t=20 min.
source: These cells in wild-type placodes could only be tracked up to t=20 min as at this point they had all invaginated into the embryo to form the initial part of the tube.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text.

claim: In hkb−/− mutants, cells near the forming central pit showed a much reduced tissue and cell shape strain rate with near identical radial and circumferential contributions.
source: In contrast, in the hkb−/− mutants, cells near the forming central pit (Figure 4A; defined to be in a 'near' position at t=0 min) showed a much reduced tissue and cell shape strain rate, with near identical radial and circumferential contributions, and constriction only commenced at about half the rate of the wild-type placodes from t=+20 min onwards (Figure 4A' and A'', dashed curves; see also Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 4A, 4A', and 4A''.

claim: In hkb−/− mutants, constriction of cells near the central pit commenced at about half the rate of wild-type placodes from t=+20 min onwards.
source: In contrast, in the hkb−/− mutants, cells near the forming central pit (Figure 4A; defined to be in a 'near' position at t=0 min) showed a much reduced tissue and cell shape strain rate, with near identical radial and circumferential contributions, and constriction only commenced at about half the rate of the wild-type placodes from t=+20 min onwards (Figure 4A' and A'', dashed curves; see also Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 4A, 4A', and 4A''.

claim: In wild-type placodes, cells far from the eccentric pit showed cell intercalations leading to circumferential convergence and radial extension of the tissue over the first approximately 20 min after invagination commenced.
source: In wild-type placodes, cells far from the eccentric pit (Figure 4B; defined to be 'far' at t=0 min), showed cell intercalations leading to circumferential convergence and radial extension of the tissue over the first approximately 20 min after invagination commenced, as we also reported previously (Figure 4B' and B'', solid curves; tissue and intercalation strain rate showing expansion radially and contraction circumferentially; Sanchez-Corrales et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 4B, 4B', and 4B'', and cites previous work.

claim: In wild-type placodes, cells far from the pit switched to apical contraction after t=+20 min once they were located closer to the pit position.
source: Interestingly, we then observed a clear switch in cell behavior of these cells to a second phase after t=+20 min. Once these cells were located closer to the pit position, they now also displayed apical contraction (beyond t=+20 min; Figure 4B' and B'', solid green curves).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 4B' and 4B''.

claim: In hkb−/− mutants, for cells at the placode periphery far from the central constriction, the tissue expanded slightly in both radial and circumferential direction.
source: In the hkb−/− mutants, for cells at the placode periphery and hence far from the central constriction (Figure 4B), the tissue expanded slightly in both radial and circumferential direction (Figure 4B' and B'', dashed gray curves)
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 4B, 4B', and 4B''.

claim: In hkb−/− mutants, cells far from the central pit showed cell shapes narrowing radially and extending circumferentially.
source: with cell shapes narrowing radially (dashed green curve in Figure 4B') and extending circumferentially (dashed green curve in Figure 4B'').
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 4B' and 4B''.

claim: In hkb−/− mutants, cells far from the central pit showed a similar rate of intercalation as in cells far from the pit in wild-type placodes.
source: We could observe a similar rate of intercalation in these cells as in cells far from the pit in wild-type placodes, with some radial elongation and circumferential contraction (dashed orange curves in Figure 4B' and B'').
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 4B' and 4B''.

claim: In wild-type placodes, circumferential neighbor gains dominate over radial neighbor gains throughout.
source: In wild-type placodes, circumferential neighbor gains outweigh radial ones by a large margin throughout (Figure 4D, dashed curves), leading to a steady increase in cumulative productive neighbor gains for cells across the placode (Figure 4E, yellow curves).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figures 4D and 4E.

claim: In hkb−/− mutant embryos, circumferential and radial neighbor gains across the placode were overall much reduced in number and occurred with equal frequency.
source: In contrast, in hkb−/− mutant embryos circumferential and radial neighbor gains across the placode were overall much reduced in number and occurred with equal frequency (Figure 4D, solid curves).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 4D.

claim: Cells near the delayed central pit in hkb−/− mutants showed no productive neighbor gains.
source: Furthermore, cells near the delayed central pit in hkb−/− mutants showed no productive neighbor gains (defined as the difference between circumferential and radial neighbor gains, corrected for the proportion of interfaces that could successfully be tracked; Figure 4E, purple dashed curve)
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 4E.

claim: Cells at the periphery away from the central pit in hkb−/− mutants showed productive neighbor gains.
source: whereas cells at the periphery away from the central pit showed productive neighbor gains (Figure 4E, solid purple curve).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 4E.

claim: Active neighbor gains in the placode are initiated and driven by junctional actomyosin.
